options.text: The amount of DNA doubles with each cycle at first, and the increase slows when a reagent becomes limiting.
options.why: Early on every molecule is copied each cycle, which gives exponential growth; later, primers or nucleotides run out, so the curve levels off.

options.text: The amount of DNA decreases in the later cycles because the polymerase destroys DNA.
options.why: The graph does not show a decrease in DNA.

options.text: The amount of DNA is constant because the original DNA is never copied.
options.why: The graph shows a large increase in DNA.

options.text: The amount of DNA increases by the same amount in every cycle for all 30 cycles.
options.why: The early part of the graph shows an increasing rate, not a constant amount of increase.

ap_biology-m22.stem: The table shows the number of individuals of each species in a community. Using the formula for Simpson's diversity index, which value is the diversity index for this community?

stimulus.description: Number of individuals of each species in a sampled community

options.why: Reports the sum of the squared proportions, Σ(n/N)² = 0.34, without subtracting it from 1.
Uses only the most abundant species: 1 − (46/123)² = 0.86.
Divides the number of species by the number of individuals: 3/123 = 0.02.

ap_biology-m23.stem: What is the surface-area-to-volume ratio of a cube-shaped cell with sides of 25 micrometers?

options.why: Uses 6s instead of 6s squared for the surface area.
Surface area = 6s² = 6(25)² = 3,750 µm² and volume = s³ = 25³ = 15,625 µm³. The ratio is 3,750 / 15,625 = 0.24 per µm.
Uses the area of one face as the surface area.

ap_biology-m24.stem: The graph shows the distribution of a heritable trait in a population before selection and after one generation of selection. Which type of selection is most consistent with the graph?

stimulus.description: Distribution of a trait in a population before and after selection

options.text: Disruptive selection, because individuals at both ends of the range were favored over intermediate ones.
options.why: After selection there is still a single peak, not two peaks near the two ends of the range.

options.text: No selection occurred, because the trait still varies after selection.
options.why: Selection can change the position or the shape of the distribution while variation remains.

options.text: Directional selection, because the whole distribution shifted toward one end of the range.
options.why: The most common value moved from about 5 before selection to about 3.75 after selection, so one end of the range was favored.

options.text: Stabilizing selection, because individuals near the middle of the range were favored.
options.why: After selection the distribution has not become narrower around 5; its peak has moved to about 3.75.

blueprint.concept: identify directional, stabilizing, or disruptive selection from distributions

ap_biology-m25.stem: The table describes the movement of ion Y across the plasma membrane. Which type of transport is most consistent with the data?

stimulus.description: Observations of the movement of ion Y across the plasma membrane of a cell

options.text: Active transport
options.why: Active transport moves a solute against its gradient using ATP, which does not match the data in the table.

options.text: Osmosis
options.why: Osmosis is the diffusion of water, and the table describes the movement of a solute instead.

options.text: Simple diffusion
options.why: The solute moves down its gradient with no protein and no ATP, which defines simple diffusion.

options.text: Facilitated diffusion
options.why: Facilitated diffusion moves a solute down its gradient with a protein and no ATP, which does not match all of the data in the table.

blueprint.subject: ap_biology
blueprint.concept: classify membrane transport from gradient direction, protein requirement, and ATP use
student_thinking: Identify the biological principle or relationship that governs the situation: classify membrane transport from gradient direction, protein requirement, and ATP use
Apply it to the information given and compare the result with the four options

key_conditions.condition: every quantity or fact needed is given in the stem or the stimulus

misconceptions.description: Active transport moves a solute against its gradient using ATP, which does not match the data in the table.
Osmosis is the diffusion of water, and the table describes the movement of a solute instead.
Facilitated diffusion moves a solute down its gradient with a protein and no ATP, which does not match all of the data in the table.
